title: Phase-aware Blocking Policy
objective: Implement shared governance config, profiles, actor authorization, structured findings, reconciliation, and phase-aware blocking from the frozen contracts.
description: Implements the runtime foundation frozen by slice-00, then turns validated provider evidence into canonical findings while keeping provider aggregates non-authoritative.
parallel_safe_reason: This slice establishes canonical finding lifecycle and blocking projections consumed by all decision slices.
must: Keep shared non-secret governance configuration in the versioned governance namespace of .quiver/config.json and preserve compatible unknown keys.
Replace blanket .quiver ignore behavior with granular runtime-only ignores where initialization owns that behavior.
Define strict versioned schemas and stable enums for profiles, actors, findings, dispositions, review events, and decisions.
Allow profile selection by CLI or shared configuration, force sensitive categories to high-assurance, propagate profile and policy identity, and reject silent downgrade.
Implement authenticated GitHub CLI provider-subject resolution separately from the versioned default-deny authorization oracle.
Read actor roles only from explicit actor_bindings and evaluate the action-specific independence rule at mutation time.
Validate provider output strictly before accepting it as contractual review evidence.
Require a validated justification whenever phase_blocking is true.
Return PROVIDER_OUTPUT_INVALID and preserve the last valid review on invalid output.
Allocate stable canonical IDs under the run lock and reconcile explicit IDs, invariant fingerprints, reopen events, and supersedes lineage.
Return FINDING_RECONCILIATION_AMBIGUOUS on multiple or incompatible matches and require an explicit disposition before an unresolved finding can close.
Compute blocking from effective profile, policy, phase, and canonical fields rather than provider aggregate.
Project current blockers, later-phase transfers, follow-ups, and optional hardening separately.
Expose plan_required_fixes, slice_required_fixes, pr_required_fixes, and follow_ups without mixing phases in required_fixes.
Apply common redaction to retained raw evidence and every rendered projection.
Add focused provider, lifecycle, policy, and failure-state tests.
acceptance: AC-01 is satisfied for shared versioned configuration, preservation, validation, and granular runtime ignores.
AC-02 is satisfied for CLI/config selection, minimum profile controls, forced high-assurance, propagation, and anti-downgrade.
AC-03 is satisfied for verified identity, explicit role bindings, action rules, independence, and default deny.
AC-04 is satisfied for stable canonical finding identity, reconciliation, collision handling, and explicit closure.
AC-05 is satisfied for deterministic phase-aware blocking and separated output categories.
A phase_blocking=true finding without valid justification is rejected.
AC-06 is satisfied for invalid provider output, preserved last valid state, and non-contractual raw evidence.
Profile policy produces deterministic results for both supported profiles and relevant phases.
Provider aggregate recommendations cannot override canonical blocking or counts.
Redaction is applied consistently before persistence and rendering.
Missing action rules, unknown actors or roles, and invalid independence values fail before mutation.
